recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if Pharmacy later decides MedicationAdministration.medication should stop allowing coded products; FHIR-5994 itself supports no current source change.
issue_request: FHIR-5994 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request from DSTU1 saying MedicationAdministration.medication was misleading because its definition said a simple medication code was possible even though a medication code was not then allowed.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-5994, but commit d406f9a2c0, described as pharmacy ballot-resolution work, changed the element from MedicationAdministration.medication Reference(Medication) 0..1 to MedicationAdministration.medication[x] CodeableConcept|Reference(Medication) 1..1 and added code-only guidance. This matches Jira's note that the issue was done as part of other tracker items.
additional_context: MedicationAdministration is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition represents MedicationAdministration.medication as CodeableReference(Medication), and current search parameter/notes source exposes both MedicationAdministration.medication.concept and MedicationAdministration.medication.reference. Later Published/Persuasive issue FHIR-25929 intentionally converted Pharmacy code-or-reference choices to CodeableReference for R5.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source changes because the original contradiction no longer exists in the current build: the definition's link-or-code wording is consistent with the current CodeableReference type.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 Pharmacy decision that converted code/reference choice attributes, including MedicationAdministration.medication, to CodeableReference.
